title: Security-service expansion: connect the California licence to the actual operator
description: Use California PPO requirements to test entity structure, qualified management, insurance and assignment readiness before promising guard coverage.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Decide which business will deliver the protection
paragraphs: Start with the service, rather than the territory description: who contracts with the client, employs and directs personnel, invoices the account and accepts a late-night incident? This guide uses California Private Patrol Operator licensing as a concrete example. It does not establish a national security licence or determine the category for alarms, investigations or armed work.

sections.heading: A new local entity changes the licence work
paragraphs: The October 2025 BSIS application packet says each entity needs its own PPO application, licences cannot be transferred or assigned to new entities, and each company licence designates a qualified manager in active charge. Selling a franchise, assigning a customer contract or authorising a brand name does not itself supply that operating authority. Record the entity and qualified person before agreeing to a coverage start date.

The packet also requires Bureau authorisation for the business name. Secretary of State name approval is not automatic BSIS name approval. Sequence the name, application, manager evidence and client-facing identity together.

sections.heading: Management independence must include the qualified role
paragraphs: A brand may be operationally repeatable while still depending on a named qualified person. Assign who supervises delivery, handles credential expiry, fills absences, escalates incidents and responds if the qualified manager leaves. Confirm replacement and continuity requirements with the Bureau instead of assuming a remote founder can absorb the role. Personnel-level registration, training and weapon-specific permissions need their own current verification before assignments; company approval is only one layer.

sections.heading: Separate minimum coverage from the account risk
paragraphs: BSIS requires PPO general liability cover of at least $1,000,000 for each occurrence and a matching certificate, maintained through licensing and renewal. Its guidance specifies occurrence cover; claims-made cover is not accepted for this requirement. These are legal operating conditions. A client’s requested additional insured status, indemnity, cyber cover or higher limit is a separate procurement and insurance question. Obtain an actual broker quote and review the contract rather than inserting the regulatory limit as the insurance budget.

sections.heading: Fictional pilot: one office contract, two operating entities
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign security brand has an experienced home-market team and a proposed California partner company. The client wants the new company to contract locally, but the plan lists only the foreign company’s credentials. The decision is to hold the promised service start, resolve the California company licence/qualified manager and name/insurance evidence, then test scheduling and incident response. The fictional example does not decide whether an exemption applies.

sections.heading: Build an assignment-readiness sheet
bullets: Identify the licensed contracting/employing entity, actual assignment address and security task.
Attach current company and responsible-person evidence; verify personnel and armed/unarmed scope separately.
Record name approval and policy/certificate dates against the same legal entity.
Cost supervisor cover, replacement staff, insurance and response duties before a royalty or territory fee.
For national accounts, decide who can accept work, who can refuse an unready assignment and who owns incident records.
Repeat the actual regulator/category review for each new state; a California file is not authority elsewhere.

practicalOutput: Entity, qualified-manager and assignment-readiness sheet
limitations: California PPO example only; exemptions, personnel/weapon credentials and branch requirements need actual current review.
No nationwide licensing, immigration, worker-classification or insurance-sufficiency opinion.

title: Staffing expansion: distinguish placements from supplying an employed workforce
description: Use NYC licensing boundaries and OSHA supplied-worker duties to build a recruitment, payroll and host-responsibility map.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Classify what the customer is buying
paragraphs: Permanent placement, executive search and supplying an agency-employed workforce have different operating facts. Write who employs the worker, pays wages, sets the assignment, invoices the client and receives a fee from the applicant. A recruitment label or a franchise agreement does not answer those questions.

sections.heading: NYC shows why the fee and employer facts matter
paragraphs: DCWP says an agency located in New York City generally needs its Employment Agency licence to provide job assistance for a fee, including helping employers find employees. It identifies a staffing agency that is the actual employer, contracts out its employees and issues them W-2 forms as outside this particular licence requirement, subject to the employer criteria. Issuing a form alone is not a general worker-classification ruling.

DCWP also identifies certain search/employer-paid agencies placing only commercial, clerical, executive, administrative and professional applicants, never charging the applicant a fee of any kind. They do not need this licence under the stated criteria, but still must comply with the applicable Employer Fee Paid Agency provisions. Do not extend this example to every job category, healthcare staffing or offices outside NYC.

sections.heading: Check the office before signing its lease
paragraphs: For a licensable NYC employment agency, DCWP’s checklist requires commercial space and says the agency cannot operate in a residential building; in a mixed building it must occupy the commercial part. The checklist also calls for the applicable bond, contracts, management information and fingerprint process. Classify the model and premises first, then assemble the relevant application evidence. The full checklist governs; this guide is not a complete application.

sections.heading: Supplying workers creates a host-safety interface
paragraphs: OSHA’s temporary-worker guidance addresses workers supplied to a host and paid by a staffing agency, whether or not the assignment is temporary. Staffing and host employers share fact-dependent safety responsibilities. OSHA recommends recording responsibilities in the contract, but the staffing agency must inquire into host conditions and verify the host fulfils its safety role. A clause saying the host handles safety does not complete that work.

Before accepting a placement, identify the actual tasks, hazards, equipment, necessary training, supervisor and incident route. Separate the agency’s general preparation from site-specific instruction and verify both. Use the applicable standards and any State Plan; the OSHA guidance does not resolve employer status under every other law.

sections.heading: Fictional pilot: solve payroll before scaling placements
paragraphs: Fictional example: a partner proposes weekly payroll for supplied warehouse workers while the customer pays accepted invoices later. The pilot model must fund wages and payroll obligations before cash arrives and must verify site/task safety before dispatch. Compare that model with an employer-paid permanent-placement service rather than use the same revenue-to-cash assumption for both. No fictional financial result or legal classification is asserted.

sections.heading: Produce one model sheet and one host file
bullets: Record actual employer, worker pay cycle, all fee flows, job classes and office location.
Resolve the relevant licence/exception and any occupation-specific staffing authority.
Allocate screening, right-to-work checks, payroll, insurance and complaint response to accountable parties; verify each legal regime separately.
For supplied workers, document the task/hazard enquiry, training evidence and host verification.
Model payroll float, invoice acceptance, disputed hours, customer concentration and replacement-worker costs.
Make account and candidate-data responsibilities explicit when the brand or national sales team sources clients.

practicalOutput: Placement-versus-staffing model sheet and host-site evidence file
limitations: NYC employment-agency example is location/category-specific and not an all-state staffing survey.
Wage, tax, employment, immigration, professional staffing, discrimination and data duties require separate applicable review.

title: Childcare expansion: sequence the California operator, premises and clearance work
description: Build a centre-opening dependency map from California’s actual licensing pathway before fixing capacity or an opening date.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Classify the care, not the brand
paragraphs: A childcare brand supplies methods and identity; the local operating plan must identify who supervises which children, at which premises, for what hours. California’s CDSS overview distinguishes home-based family childcare from centres and identifies circumstances in which care and supervision of non-relative children from more than one family will likely need a licence. The word likely matters: statutory exemptions require their own factual analysis.

sections.heading: A centre and a family home are different planning branches
paragraphs: CDSS describes a family childcare home as the licensee’s own home and a centre as usually commercial premises. Both descriptions concern non-medical care for periods shorter than 24 hours. Do not treat a retail lease, a tutoring label or a school-age programme as proof of exemption. Record ages, care/supervision, duration, actual operator and premises, then confirm the category and applicable exceptions with the responsible office.

sections.heading: Use the real opening sequence
paragraphs: The CDSS centre pathway requires two-part orientation before application, then a complete application and supporting documents. Background checks, entity/compliance history, financial verification, local fire clearance and a pre-licensing inspection sit in the process. The local fire authority is a separate dependency; the licensing analyst requests its clearance. A signed lease or a pending facility number is not the final licence.

The process document makes timing conditional on complete appropriate materials, clearances and a compliant facility. Treat alterations, missing documents and background issues as schedule risks. Do not promise a fixed opening date from a processing target measured only after completeness.

sections.heading: Turn capacity into an evidence-dependent operating plan
paragraphs: Before pricing the centre, resolve age-specific capacity, staffing qualifications/ratios, supervision cover and physical-space requirements from the current applicable rules. This guide does not provide those numbers. Allocate responsibility for recruitment, safeguarding, clearances, incident reporting, attendance and the records that must remain available to the regulator. Budget the actual director/supervisor and absence cover before a royalty or management fee.

sections.heading: Fictional pilot: the lease is ready, the clearance path is not
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign education brand and a California partner choose premises for a combined learning-and-care programme. Their draft schedule assumes teaching can begin when fit-out ends. The practical decision is to define the supervision/age/hour facts, resolve the licensing category, map local fire and licensing dependencies and obtain the actual staffing/capacity requirements before making parent commitments. The fictional facts do not establish a licence exemption.

sections.heading: Create the opening dependency map
bullets: Name the applicant/operator, centre/home category, children’s ages and supervision hours.
Document the specific exemption basis or required licence pathway; do not infer exemption from a programme name.
Assign orientation, application completeness and corrections to one accountable manager.
Track required background clearances against the people and permitted presence/work.
Link premises alterations, local fire clearance and licensing inspection milestones.
Keep capacity, staffing and opening-date assumptions unresolved until supported by the relevant current rules and approvals.

practicalOutput: Childcare category, staffing-evidence and opening dependency map
limitations: California example only, not a complete licence application or all-state child-care analysis.
Age-specific ratios, capacity, personnel qualifications, additional local permissions and medical services are not determined here.

title: Education-centre expansion: classify the learner and California approval pathway
description: Distinguish adult education approval, a supported exemption and credential marketing using California’s 2026 postsecondary Act.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Separate adult education from school and childcare
paragraphs: An education centre can teach children, prepare adults for employment or provide recreational learning. These are different regulatory questions. This guide examines the California private postsecondary route for an actual adult-education business; it does not clear K–12, childcare, an occupational qualification or another state.

sections.heading: Identify the institution before choosing the franchise structure
paragraphs: California Education Code 94857 defines postsecondary education by the intended learners and programme, including academic, vocational and continuing professional education. Section 94858 describes a private entity physically present in California offering that education to the public for an institutional charge. Identify the entity running the centre, the learner cohort, the complete programme, what is charged and the credential offered. A standard curriculum or foreign accreditation does not decide those elements.

Section 94886 generally requires approval before opening, conducting or doing business as the covered institution, subject to exemptions and stated transition provisions. Resolve that pathway before presales and student recruitment, rather than treat the operating approval as a post-launch administrative task.

sections.heading: Use the exact exemption, not an attractive label
paragraphs: Section 94874 contains distinct conditions. Examples include solely avocational/recreational programmes, certain postsecondary admission-test preparation and specified approved/certified/sponsored continuing education or licence-exam preparation. The complete statutory conditions and cross-referenced limits matter. Calling a course a workshop, requiring nominal membership or issuing a certificate does not automatically establish an exemption.

The Act also provides an optional Bureau verification process for an exempt institution; a verification remains dependent on continued compliance with its conditions. Do not turn an exemption into a claim of state endorsement. Evaluate an added vocational course, a changed audience, tuition/funding or a new credential before reusing an earlier status analysis.

sections.heading: Review the student promise separately from the partner pitch
paragraphs: For institutions subject to the cited fair-business-practice provisions, section 94897 prohibits promising or guaranteeing employment and overstating job availability; advertising about jobs, skills or learning time must be accurate and not misleading. It also controls accreditation and approval wording. Approval is not a state recommendation or proof of exceeding minimum state standards.

Keep two evidence files: the institutional/credential/advertising file for students and the franchise-classification/disclosure file for prospective business partners. One does not replace the other. Any employment-outcome material used in either must be assessed for the applicable audience and legal regime.

sections.heading: Fictional pilot: a new vocational course changes the question
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign brand offers recreational workshops and plans to add a paid adult course marketed as preparation for a new career. Management cannot assume the original recreational analysis continues to apply to the whole institution. Freeze the new advertising, describe all programmes and credentials, check the current statutory conditions and resolve approval or exemption before offering the changed model. No fictional school or employment result is represented as real.

sections.heading: Prepare a programme-to-authority matrix
bullets: Record learner stage, course purpose, programme length, teaching location and actual operating/charging entity.
List every course, credential, total charge and funding source; evaluate the institution’s full offering.
Attach the exact exemption conditions and limitations or the applicable approval route/evidence.
Separate BPPE authority from accreditation, occupational licensure and credential recognition.
Check job, skill, duration and approval/accreditation claims against current evidence and statutory status.
Add local premises/use and staffing requirements as separate evidence tasks before committing to an opening date.

practicalOutput: Programme-to-authority matrix and student-claims evidence file
limitations: California private postsecondary physical-presence example only; other education, online/out-of-state and local regimes require separate review.
Not an exemption determination, accreditation verification or professional credential approval.

title: California janitorial registration: map the provider, franchisee and customer roles
description: Contractors and franchisees can be covered workers. Identify each entity’s role before assuming a cleaning network is outside employer registration.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A franchise structure does not answer the registration question
paragraphs: California’s Labor Commissioner describes a janitorial employer as a person or entity employing a covered worker or engaging through contracts, subcontracts or franchise arrangements for covered janitorial services. A covered worker can be an employee, independent contractor or franchisee predominantly working as a janitor. The FAQ expressly includes a commercial cleaning provider without employees and a provider using franchisees or contractors.

For an overseas cleaning brand, map the U.S. contracting entity, local provider, franchisee and actual individuals doing the work. Calling the workers independent businesses does not establish an exclusion from this specific registration program.

sections.heading: Separate the service provider from the service recipient
paragraphs: The agency FAQ excludes a business acting as the recipient of cleaning services, illustrated by a restaurant hiring a cleaner after closing. It also excludes a provider that only cleans residential dwellings and states the agency’s interpretation for public entities. Those examples depend on the actual role and work; they do not create a general exemption for an intermediary arranging commercial cleaning.

sections.heading: Build the filing and renewal packet around the actual entity
paragraphs: The current program states a $500 nonrefundable initial application fee and $500 annual renewal. Registration lasts one year and renewal is due by the original issuance month and day. Section 13810 asks for customer and contractor/franchisee information as well as entity details; workers’ compensation evidence is conditional on employing one or more employees.
bullets: Assign each provider’s legal name, business names, ownership information and relevant entity documents.
List the customers and contractors or franchisees the application calls for, with registration details where applicable.
Preserve registration evidence and expiry dates; review a counterparty’s registration when entering, extending, renewing or modifying a janitorial contract.
Assign the required three-year employee and other covered-worker records, including work periods and compensation.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the customer contract and the operating contract differ
paragraphs: A Singapore facilities brand signs a California office-cleaning contract through its U.S. subsidiary and allocates the work to a local franchisee. The office is the service recipient. The subsidiary and franchisee need their own role and registration assessment; the recipient example does not automatically exempt either provider. The practical output is a two-row provider schedule with the actual contract, workers, registration owner and evidence.

sections.heading: Keep the separate compliance tracks visible
paragraphs: This janitorial registration does not decide whether the business model is a franchise under sales laws, whether individuals are employees for another purpose, or which wages apply. Janitorial training also has its own provider, timing and record requirements. Maintain those as separate tasks before staffing or selling the model.

practicalOutput: An entity-by-entity janitorial registration schedule with role facts, filing evidence, renewal date and a three-year records owner.
limitations: This is a source-reviewed guide to its named issue, not a complete employment, franchise, tax, licensing or local-law survey.
Apply the actual entity, worksite, worker, industry and date facts. No worker classification, exemption or transaction is approved by this guide.

title: California janitorial harassment-prevention training: own the deadline and proof
description: Build the required sexual violence and harassment prevention training cycle, qualified-provider route and records for covered janitorial workers and supervisors.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the covered workforce
paragraphs: The janitorial program’s covered-worker definition can include contractors and franchisees predominantly performing janitorial work, as well as employees. The program’s sexual violence and harassment prevention training covers nonsupervisory covered workers and their supervisors. A network should identify the actual people and responsible employer rather than assume a franchise agreement supplies completed training.

sections.heading: Calendar both the new-position deadline and the recurring cycle
paragraphs: Section 13821 requires at least two hours at least once every two years and training within six months of assuming a new covered position. Segments may be separated, but each must last at least one hour. The regulation has a specific covered-successor rule for qualifying retained workforces; acquiring a contract alone does not establish its conditions.

sections.heading: Use the prescribed route and understandable content
paragraphs: DIR’s current program says in-person compliance must begin following publication of the qualified-organization list in January 2024. Its FAQ distinguishes qualified peer trainers for nonsupervisory workers from qualified supervisor trainers. The required content is developed through LOHP under DIR’s direction, and training must match the language and literacy understood by the participants. A general online orientation is not evidence that these requirements were met.

sections.heading: The employer keeps the proof even when another entity trains
paragraphs: The regulation places the proof burden on the employer, including when another entity or janitorial employer provides training. Keep the required records for at least three years and make them available to the Labor Commissioner.
bullets: Record participant names, covered roles, position-start dates, training dates and next due dates.
Keep printed names and signatures at both the start and completion, certificates, content and provider identity.
Retain the signed DLSE 800 compliance form and required certification concerning payment of the qualified organization.
Provide a trainee’s materials and attendance or completion certificate when requested.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a newly appointed route supervisor
paragraphs: A local operator promotes a cleaner to a supervisory role and receives a spreadsheet saying the worker attended an old customer video. The compliance owner records the new role date, checks the six-month requirement and applicable prior-training facts, verifies the qualified provider and content, and collects the actual evidence. An unsupported “trained” tick does not close the task.

practicalOutput: A covered-worker training register with position-start date, due date, qualified provider, required materials and a three-year evidence folder.
limitations: This is a source-reviewed guide to its named issue, not a complete employment, franchise, tax, licensing or local-law survey.

title: California pay planning: check the wage floor and the manager’s actual duties
description: Use the 2026 general minimum as a starting point, then test location, industry and any claimed executive exemption independently.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The 2026 state floor is not the final worksite rate
paragraphs: California’s MW-2026 sets the general minimum at $16.90 per hour from January 1, 2026. The order has applicability limits and separate fast-food and healthcare tracks; DIR also explains that local requirements can be higher. Map every actual worksite and industry before pricing a service contract. A metropolitan label or headquarters address does not establish all worksite requirements.

sections.heading: A manager title does not establish the executive exemption
paragraphs: DLSE describes cumulative conditions involving enterprise or recognized-unit management, regular direction of two or more employees, hiring or firing authority or weighted recommendations, discretion and independent judgment, primarily exempt duties, and the required salary. Compare the planned role with the work actually done, especially where a launch manager will spend substantial time cleaning, delivering services or following a prescribed manual.

sections.heading: Separate the salary calculation from the employment budget
paragraphs: The executive entry describes a monthly salary of at least twice the state minimum for full-time employment and identifies a 40-hour full-time week. Using the 2026 general minimum gives an annualized planning equivalent of $70,304: $16.90 × 40 × 52 × 2. This is an arithmetic illustration of that salary component, not a finding that any worker is exempt or that every industry uses this exact screen.

A fully loaded employment budget can include employer taxes, benefits, insurance, recruitment and equipment. Those budget entries are not automatically the guaranteed salary tested by the exemption. Keep the actual salary terms and the duties analysis separate.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a $120,000 employment budget
paragraphs: An expansion plan allows $120,000 for the first local manager but allocates $65,000 to base salary and the balance to employer costs and launch support. The total budget does not satisfy the illustrated $70,304 salary component. Raising salary alone would still leave the actual executive duties to assess. The finance owner should model the correct pay basis and applicable overtime rather than assume the title resolves it.

sections.heading: Keep an evidence packet before making the offer
bullets: Actual worksite addresses, service industry and applicable wage order.
The rate source, its effective period and any higher local or industry requirement.
Actual duties, expected time allocation, reporting lines and authority over staff.
Guaranteed base salary, pay schedule and employer-cost assumptions as separate entries.
A recheck before a later payroll year or material role change; this guide does not supply a 2027 California rate.

practicalOutput: A dated worksite-rate check and a separate manager-duty assessment, with base salary distinguished from total employer cost.
limitations: This is a source-reviewed guide to its named issue, not a complete employment, franchise, tax, licensing or local-law survey.
Apply the actual entity, worksite, worker, industry and date facts. No worker classification, exemption or transaction is approved by this guide.

title: Texas contractor planning: test control for unemployment tax before using a 1099
description: TWC considers actual working facts and the right to control. Build evidence for each role instead of treating a contractor label as the result.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the test being answered
paragraphs: The Texas Workforce Commission’s guidance addresses the Texas Unemployment Compensation Act. It identifies service, wages and direction or control, and explains that the right to control can be enough even if it is not exercised. An agreement, business name or IRS form does not determine that classification. This is a specific unemployment-tax inquiry; federal wage law and federal tax law need their own analysis.

sections.heading: The twenty factors are evidence prompts, not a points game
paragraphs: TWC’s comparative guide looks at instructions, training, integration, personal service, helpers, continuing relationships, set hours, full-time requirements, work location, sequence, reports, payment, expenses, tools, investment, profit or loss, multiple clients, public availability, discharge and quitting. TWC says not every factor applies and the weight of a factor can change with the business and facts.
bullets: Record who can decide the methods and sequence of work, assign hours and require attendance or training.
Identify who supplies tools, pays expenses, hires substitutes or helpers and bears the risk of an unprofitable job.
Check actual customer availability, repeat engagements and termination rights against the written contract.
Attach examples from operations, invoices, schedules and manuals; explain disputed facts rather than count favorable answers.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a controlled service route
paragraphs: A facilities company calls a worker a contractor but fixes the route, dictates the cleaning sequence, supplies equipment, requires its training and pays a fixed weekly amount. Those facts raise the control issues identified by TWC; a 1099 does not resolve them. A useful review compares each relevant fact, the retained contractual rights and the real performance, then records the classification rationale or obtains TWC assistance.

sections.heading: Close the payroll task only for the reviewed scope
paragraphs: Give a responsible person the actual Texas unemployment-tax assessment and supporting facts before payroll or contractor onboarding. Record changes when the worker gains or loses genuine control or financial independence. Do not carry the result across other states or legal regimes without checking their own tests.

practicalOutput: A Texas unemployment-tax classification memo that links control facts to evidence and keeps other legal tests open.
limitations: This is a source-reviewed guide to its named issue, not a complete employment, franchise, tax, licensing or local-law survey.
Apply the actual entity, worksite, worker, industry and date facts. No worker classification, exemption or transaction is approved by this guide.

title: New York wage planning: select the region, industry and payroll period
description: The dated 2026 posters distinguish regional rates and building-service arrangements. A statewide rate or a cleaning label is not enough.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use the actual work location and a dated source
paragraphs: NYDOL’s miscellaneous-industry and building-service posters for January 1 through December 31, 2026 show $17 per hour in New York City, Long Island and Westchester County, and $16 in the rest of the state. An Albany worksite and a Westchester worksite therefore require different regional entries even when the same company supplies staff.

sections.heading: Identify the wage order before copying a cleaning budget
paragraphs: The building-service poster separately addresses residential janitor pay by unit or weekly salary and includes a residential-janitor overtime exception. The miscellaneous poster has its own extra-pay and credit notes. A commercial cleaning business should establish the actual industry and role rather than apply a residential janitor provision merely because a person cleans buildings.

The posters also flag matters beyond an hourly minimum, including overtime, uniform maintenance and, where applicable, call-in pay or spread of hours. The miscellaneous poster says no tip credit is available; do not import a restaurant’s hospitality credit into a different wage order. This guide does not decide any overtime exemption.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the same service in two regions
paragraphs: A business budgets 30 covered hours each week for a worker at a Westchester office and another worker at an Albany office. Using only the cited general 2026 hourly floors gives $510 and $480 in weekly base wages respectively, before other required pay and employer costs. The $30 difference is a planning illustration, not a complete payroll estimate or permission to ignore the correct wage order.

sections.heading: Keep the 2027 announcement separate from a proposal
paragraphs: As read for this review, the NYDOL overview displays a 2027 table and announces that the standard $17/$16 rates will stay unchanged under an off-ramp. It separately announces a home-care increase and describes a Governor’s proposal to alter the off-ramp provisions. An announced administrative explanation and a legislative proposal are different evidence. Use the dated 2026 posters for 2026 work and recheck enacted law and current agency guidance before 2027 payroll.

sections.heading: What the payroll owner should retain
bullets: Actual worksite, geographic region and payroll period.
Industry wage order and actual worker category, including any residential-janitor facts.
Dated rate source and the review of overtime, uniforms, call-in pay, spread of hours and any claimed credit.
Separate employer taxes, insurance, benefits and other operating costs from base wages.
Unresolved category or exemption questions assigned to a named reviewer before relying on a lower figure.

practicalOutput: A worksite-by-worksite payroll sheet with the correct region, industry order, worker category, rate period and extra-pay questions.

title: Real case: Premier Martial Arts allegations test the evidence behind semi-absentee claims
description: Read the FTC’s 2026 PFG and Franchise Fastlane complaint as a practical test of owner hours, comparable earnings cohorts and outside sales-management roles; proposed settlements are not treated as entered judgments.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
label: Real filed case: allegations and proposed settlements; court entry not verified
practicalOutput: Owner-hours evidence file, cohort-comparability matrix and external-sales responsibility review
limitations: The complaint contains FTC allegations; this guide does not find the alleged conduct proved.
FTC index was checked and lists Pending; no entered final order, current complete court docket, payment, refund or individual cancellation entitlement is verified.
The allegations concern specific parties, offerings and historical periods; they do not establish that every semi-absentee or management-run model is unlawful or unworkable.

sections.heading: Know exactly what was reviewed
paragraphs: This is a real federal case, FTC v. Premier Franchising Group, LLC and Franchise Fastlane, LLC, case 3:26-cv-00487 in the Eastern District of Tennessee. The complete 53-page complaint is stamped filed 5 October 2026. Premier Franchising Group (PFG) is identified as franchisor of Premier Martial Arts (PMA); Franchise Fastlane (FFL) as its former franchise sales organisation. The factual account below reports the FTC’s allegations, not court findings.

At review on 12 November 2026 Pacific time, the FTC case index, last updated 13 October 2026, labelled the matter Pending. Both posted stipulated-order PDFs were reviewed through their complete operative bodies and signatures; PFG’s proposed franchisee notice was also read. The judicial signature/date fields in those copies are blank. Court entry or a later disposition has not been independently verified, so this page describes proposed settlements and does not state that a judgment was entered or money collected.

sections.heading: The alleged operating promise matters as much as the number
paragraphs: The FTC alleges PFG and FFL marketed profitable semi-absentee ownership to people without martial-arts experience, often with claims of fewer than 15 hours a week from the beginning. It alleges the sellers lacked evidence that these new operators could run the proposed studios profitably on that basis. The complaint also describes new owners reporting much more work than expected. These allegations appear particularly in paragraphs 134–150.

For a business preparing a management-run model, the useful question is what the evidence actually measures. Record founder and owner work during launch and mature trading, the local manager’s tasks and paid hours, instructor/customer-acquisition duties, absence cover and escalation. A statement that a manager can be hired is not evidence of the owner’s remaining workload or the cost of replacing the founder’s skills.

sections.heading: Ask whether the earnings cohort matches the business being sold
paragraphs: The complaint contrasts experienced owner-operators of established, often larger Legacy studios with New Franchisees recruited into a smaller-studio, semi-absentee model. It alleges material differences in experience, studio size, contract obligations, curriculum autonomy and fees, along with selective inclusion of earnings data and some combined multi-studio data presented as a single studio. Those are allegations about comparability and data construction, not merely disagreement about a percentage.

A concrete pleaded comparison is the 2022 FDD’s stated 2021 average EBITDA of $75,950 for the combined studio group versus $17,584 for New Franchisee studios alleged in paragraph 118. These are historical figures reported in the complaint, not this site’s verified unit accounts, a current earnings forecast or a claim that another brand will obtain those results.

Current Item 19 requires reasonable basis and written substantiation when an FPR is made, with the relevant historical cohort details or forecast assumptions. The case makes those questions operational: ask why included outlets are comparable, how incomplete/closed/new units are treated, whether each record represents one unit and how costs change for the proposed owner/manager model.

sections.heading: Bring the sales channel into the same evidence review
paragraphs: The FTC alleges break-even and individual-studio earnings claims were disseminated in calls, recordings and other material outside the relevant Item 19 disclosures. It also alleges PFG omitted FFL personnel from Item 2 despite their management responsibility for franchise sales. The complaint describes FFL managing recruitment/development, calls and discovery activity, while PFG retained approval and review roles. See paragraphs 30–39,122–133 and 195–197.

Item 2 concerns individuals with management responsibility relating to franchise sale or operation, as well as the prescribed business experience. Map what an external sales organisation actually does rather than assume the word external removes the issue. Preserve the current FDD, scripts, recordings, presentations and approvals; reconcile claims and responsible people before the next sales campaign. This is an evidence review, not a finding that every broker has the same role as alleged here.

sections.heading: What the proposed papers establish, and what they do not
paragraphs: Both proposed orders contain non-admission language and proposed restrictions addressing income/sales, break-even time, owner hours and semi-absentee representations, plus Franchise Rule compliance. PFG’s proposal additionally contains a cancellation-notice mechanism for a defined group; it excludes Legacy Franchisees, certain settling claimants and transferee franchisees. The documents have detailed monetary and compliance provisions, but their presence in a proposed filing does not establish court entry, payment or a refund.

Do not infer that any reader can cancel now, that notice has been delivered or that all franchisees have the same rights. The actual operative entered order, eligibility facts, notice and later procedural record would have to be checked for that purpose. No amount awarded, collected or distributed is asserted here.

sections.heading: Use the case to make a reviewable decision
paragraphs: Produce three linked outputs before promoting a hands-off or management-run opportunity: an owner-hours evidence file, a cohort-comparability matrix and an external-sales responsibility review. Keep observed facts, assumptions and unresolved items separate. If the existing data describes expert owner-operators in a materially different format, either substantiate the proposed claim with appropriate evidence or stop using it while the gap is investigated.
bullets: Describe the exact proposed operator, required skills, premises format and owner/manager participation at launch and maturity.
For every financial claim, identify the period, unit population, inclusion/exclusion rules, one-unit versus combined records, costs and written substantiation.
Explain material differences between reference units and the offered model rather than rely on a system-wide average.
Audit hours, break-even and earnings language across calls, recordings, websites, broker decks and the current FDD.
Identify internal and external people with actual franchise-sales or operating management responsibility for Item 2 review.
Keep the pending-case/proposed-order status attached when using this real case in internal training; do not turn allegations into findings.

title: Give franchise brokers a controlled sales workflow
description: Map each seller, permitted claims and disclosure handoffs before paying for introductions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the seller, the speaker and the duty
paragraphs: Section 436.1 uses a broad franchise-seller definition: franchisors, relevant employees, representatives and agents, subfranchisors and third-party brokers involved in sales. Section 436.9 addresses prohibited seller conduct. The separate disclosure-timing provision places the FDD delivery obligation on the franchisor. Do not compress those different actors into “the broker handles compliance.”

sections.heading: Control the actual sales channels
paragraphs: A referral agreement is only one part of the record. Review presentations, broker portals, webinars, private messages and conversations about likely sales or profit. Sellers must not contradict required disclosures or misrepresent a reference as independent. Financial-performance claims require the rule’s basis, substantiation and disclosure conditions.
bullets: Record each speaker, contracting entity, channel, compensation and permitted territory.
Give the broker approved materials and a named escalation contact for earnings questions.
Keep a versioned record of what was said and which FDD was delivered, with actual dates.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a cleaning-brand introduction
paragraphs: A broker calls a proposed partner a “territory investor” and says a local manager can deliver a predictable margin. Calling the meeting an introduction does not remove a sales claim. The expansion lead should preserve the exact statement, stop its reuse pending review, compare it with Item 19 and route the corrected material through the disclosure owner. This example establishes a review task, not that a particular sale violated the rule.

sections.heading: Output and unresolved gates
paragraphs: Build a seller-responsibility sheet showing who approves materials, supplies the current FDD, records delivery, answers claims questions and checks the relevant states. No offer should rely on the sheet as state sales authorization.

practicalOutput: A seller map, controlled claim library and documented disclosure handoff.
limitations: Federal seller definition and prohibited conduct only; state broker/licensing and sales-authorization requirements are not researched here.

title: Review franchise advertising against the actual disclosure record
description: Separate an ordinary brand message from a performance claim and preserve the exact version used.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The wording and context matter
paragraphs: The relevant record is the advertisement that a prospective partner actually sees. Federal seller prohibitions apply to oral, visual and written representations. A disclaimer or broker label does not cure a contradiction with required disclosures. An earnings or sales number must be checked against the financial-performance rules and the actual Item 19, rather than justified by a promising home-market result.

sections.heading: Use a short claim register
paragraphs: List each quantitative or implied performance claim, the corresponding disclosed statement, the population and period used, and the written support. Preserve the image, caption, landing page and spoken presentation together.
bullets: Record gross revenue versus profit, included and excluded units, geography and operating model.
Identify testimonials, reference incentives and any asserted independence.
When a source number changes, locate every live version rather than editing one presentation only.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a home-market margin slide
paragraphs: A technical-services brand has one home-country unit with a 20% operating margin and puts “target 20%” in a U.S. recruitment deck. Renaming an achieved number a target does not answer whether the context makes it a performance representation or whether there is a reasonable basis for the U.S. claim. Finance must identify comparability gaps and the disclosure lead must decide whether the slide can be used. This is a fictional review example, not an approved claim.

sections.heading: Keep a release decision
paragraphs: For each version, record approved, revise or pause, the person responsible and the unresolved evidence. Recheck independent state advertising and sales requirements before releasing the campaign. Reading this guide is not campaign approval.

practicalOutput: A versioned advertising-claim register with substantiation and an accountable release decision.
limitations: Does not decide a particular advertisement or authorize state sales. Current state advertising filing and legend rules remain open.

title: Check customer-provision promises against the Business Opportunity Rule
description: An established seller still needs to examine the purchaser’s new business and the promises being sold.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Ask whose business is new
paragraphs: Part 437’s new-business question concerns the prospective purchaser. A seller that has operated for many years cannot dismiss the rule merely because its own business is established. The definition also requires a payment and specified representations that the seller or a designated person will provide locations, accounts/customers or buy back what the purchaser produces.

sections.heading: Distinguish customer supply from ordinary advice
paragraphs: The definition can reach recommended lead-generation or locator services, customer lists and some payment-collection arrangements. General business-development advice, training and advertising alone are not treated as providing customers under that definition. Capture the exact promise and actual arrangement rather than treating every marketing service alike.

sections.heading: A separate disclosure clock, with an unresolved intersection
paragraphs: For an arrangement within Part 437, §437.2 requires the prescribed written disclosure and applicable earnings information at least seven calendar days before the earlier binding agreement or payment/other consideration. Section 437.7 separately requires specified disclosure versions, receipts, contracts and earnings support to be retained for three years.

Important source conflict: the current text of §437.8 uses a $500 figure while cross-referencing the minimum-payment franchise exemption in §436.8(a)(1), whose current threshold is different. This guide does not resolve that interaction, update one text by assumption or conclude an exemption applies. Record it as an unresolved scope gate.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: A facilities brand sells an established local operator a new cleaning line, required software and a promise of named customer accounts. The fact that both companies already exist does not alone answer the new-line/new-business question. Prepare a factsheet with the purchaser’s activity, payment schedule, exact accounts promise, classification review and applicable disclosure clock before accepting money.

practicalOutput: A Part437 scope factsheet, promise inventory and unresolved franchise-exemption question.
limitations: The literal $500/§436.8(a)(1) cross-reference interaction is unresolved; no exemption conclusion is provided.
State business-opportunity and franchise laws require independent review.

title: Separate company formation from permission to do business in another state
description: Create a state-activity register before assuming one incorporation filing covers the operating footprint.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: “Foreign” can mean another U.S. state
paragraphs: For qualification purposes, an entity formed in one U.S. state can be foreign in another. This is a different use of the word from the owner’s citizenship or an overseas parent. SBA describes possible certificates of authority and, in many states, evidence of good standing. It directs businesses to the individual state offices for requirements and fees.

sections.heading: Map activities before choosing a filing answer
paragraphs: For each entity, record employees and their work locations, premises, customer service, contract performance and intended state expansion. Ask the relevant state office or adviser to apply the actual statutory test. A national website, a single customer or an owner’s address should not be converted into a universal qualification rule here.
bullets: Keep formation, qualification, tax accounts and sector permits in separate columns.
Record the legal entity that employs staff and signs each local contract.
Assign annual-report and registered-agent responsibilities where applicable.

sections.heading: Fictional example: formation in Delaware, operations elsewhere
paragraphs: A Singapore-owned company forms a Delaware LLC but proposes a staffed service depot in Texas. Delaware formation is evidence of entity creation; it does not answer Texas qualification, payroll tax, customer-site licences or the depot’s occupancy conditions. The practical next step is a Texas activity dossier and a dated requirement check, not a second unsupported incorporation recommendation.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Create one register per operating entity, with formation documents, each additional-state activity, the authority consulted, filing decision, evidence and recurring owner. Keep unresolved qualification explicitly unresolved.

practicalOutput: An entity-by-state activity and qualification register with separate tax and permit workstreams.
limitations: SBA overview only; no individual state threshold, exemption, filing fee or tax-nexus determination was researched.

title: An LLC’s legal form does not settle its federal tax classification
description: Prepare the ownership, default classification and election dates before filing Form 8832.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Separate three questions
paragraphs: State-law entity form, federal tax classification and the owner’s immigration position answer different questions. A domestic eligible entity with two or more members generally defaults to partnership classification; a single-owner eligible entity generally defaults to disregarded status unless an election applies. The foreign-entity defaults differ and depend in part on limited liability. Do not copy the domestic default onto the overseas parent.

sections.heading: An election has a dated procedure
paragraphs: Section 301.7701-3 and the Form 8832 instructions govern eligible-entity elections. The ordinary effective-date window is up to 75 days before filing and up to 12 months after filing. A change election generally has a 60-month restriction, with exceptions; an initial election effective on formation is treated differently. Late relief has conditions and is not assumed. The retrieved form is revision December 2013, not a newly issued 2026 form.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a wholly foreign-owned LLC
paragraphs: An overseas company forms a one-member domestic LLC and assumes “disregarded” means no U.S. information return. Classification alone does not answer Form 5472 and related pro-forma return obligations for reportable transactions. The CFO should record the owner, entity, transactions and proposed election before obtaining a filing conclusion. This example does not recommend a tax structure or assert a specific return is due.

sections.heading: Output and responsibilities
paragraphs: Prepare an entity-classification brief with the exact legal entity, jurisdiction, owners, liability characteristics, default, intended treatment, effective date, EIN and returns affected. Finance owns the dates; a tax reviewer decides the applicable election and reporting position.

practicalOutput: An entity-classification and election-date brief, linked to separate foreign-owned reporting tasks.
limitations: Not a recommendation to form an LLC or elect corporate/partnership treatment. No tax savings, treaty or immigration result is promised.

title: Build evidence for royalties and services between related companies
description: A percentage copied from a partner contract is not a transfer-pricing method.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the controlled transactions
paragraphs: A foreign parent may license a brand, provide remote support, lend working capital and supply products to its U.S. affiliate. Those are distinct transactions with different facts. Section 1.482-1 asks whether the results are consistent with dealings between uncontrolled taxpayers in comparable circumstances. “Our standard royalty is 6%” is not itself evidence that the controlled arrangement is arm’s length.

sections.heading: Prepare facts before choosing a method
paragraphs: The best-method rule seeks the most reliable measure under the facts and circumstances; it does not provide a universal first-choice percentage. Reliability depends on comparability, data quality and assumptions. Services and intangibles have additional method provisions outside this scoped review.
bullets: Document who develops, owns, funds and maintains the IP.
List actual support deliverables, staff time, costs and who benefits.
Identify operating functions, assets and risks in each entity.
Keep third-party comparables separate from internal policy rates and explain material differences.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a service bundle
paragraphs: A European parent invoices its new U.S. subsidiary one royalty covering brand use, training and quarterly technical support. A useful first output separates the rights and services, shows the staff and costs, and records the U.S. entity’s actual functions. It does not assume every cost is chargeable, that all services are one transaction, or that a franchisee’s unrelated-party rate can be copied without adjustment.

sections.heading: Give finance an evidence ledger
paragraphs: Record the agreement, actual conduct, method question, data source, allocation assumptions, invoice and payment currency. Transfer-pricing support and withholding compliance are separate workstreams; neither is established by a well-written intercompany contract alone.

practicalOutput: A controlled-transaction evidence ledger and specific method/comparability questions for tax review.
limitations: Review limited to §1.482-1(a)–(c); transaction-specific methods, documentation rules, treaties and foreign-country transfer pricing are not comprehensively researched.

title: Separate a U.S. business visit from doing the operating work
description: Turn a proposed founder trip into an activity schedule instead of inferring work permission from company ownership.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The activity is the starting point
paragraphs: An owner can remain abroad and still plan meetings with a proposed U.S. partner. The State Department lists consulting with business associates, attending relevant conferences and negotiating contracts among B-1 business examples. It separately lists employment as prohibited on visitor visas. Owning a U.S. company or receiving payment overseas does not by itself settle which side a planned activity falls on.

sections.heading: Describe the trip precisely
paragraphs: Write what happens each day, who receives the benefit, who performs the work and how the traveller is paid. “Launch support” is too vague when it might mean investor meetings, interviewing a manager, training staff or servicing a customer. These activities should not be treated as interchangeable.
bullets: Separate negotiation and observation from hands-on delivery or ordinary management work.
Identify the host, customer sites, proposed duration and repeat-visit pattern.
Keep the evidence and unresolved activity question with the trip owner.

sections.heading: Fictional example: the technical founder
paragraphs: A founder proposes three days negotiating a distribution contract followed by two weeks repairing customer equipment alongside the new team. The meeting examples do not establish permission for the repair work. Split the itinerary and obtain an activity-specific answer before booking the operational portion. This guide does not decide that a particular alternative visa is available.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Produce a visit-activity brief with permitted-purpose evidence and unresolved tasks. A visa does not guarantee admission; the admitting authorities decide entry. Keep any L-1, E-2 or other work-authorised staffing plan as its own workstream.

practicalOutput: A dated trip-activity brief separating meetings from unresolved operational work.
limitations: No individual visa, ESTA, admission, productive-training or hands-on service conclusion is provided.

title: Budget a hired manager and team using the federal workweek rules
description: Check coverage and nonexempt hours before converting a home-market labour percentage into a U.S. plan.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Do not use $500,000 as a universal escape
paragraphs: DOL Fact Sheet 14 distinguishes enterprise coverage from individual coverage. The ordinary enterprise test includes at least two employees and at least $500,000 in annual business volume, while specified institutions have different coverage treatment. Individual interstate-commerce coverage can apply even if the enterprise does not meet that volume. A small launch budget is not a no-wage-law conclusion.

sections.heading: Use the workweek, not a monthly average
paragraphs: Fact Sheet 23 explains overtime for covered nonexempt employees after 40 hours in a fixed 168-hour workweek. Averaging a busy week with a quiet week is not permitted. Paying a salary does not itself remove overtime rights, and an advance-approval policy does not waive overtime already earned. This guide does not quote a current salary-exemption threshold or determine who qualifies for an exemption.

sections.heading: Fictional worked example: 45 hours
paragraphs: Assume a covered, nonexempt technician works 45 hours at a $20 regular hourly rate, with no other compensation affecting that rate. Straight-time pay is 45 × $20 = $900; the additional overtime premium is 5 × $10 = $50, for $950 total before employer burden. This is fictional arithmetic, not a local wage quotation or a complete regular-rate calculation. A second week of 35 hours does not erase the first week’s overtime.

sections.heading: Build the staffing evidence
paragraphs: Record the employer, actual duties, reporting lines, weekly schedule, all compensation components and timekeeping owner. Add separate state/local wage, leave and tax-account tasks. Keep an exemption or worker-status question unresolved until the relevant facts and current rules have been checked.

practicalOutput: A weekly staffing-cost worksheet with coverage, duties, regular-rate and local-law questions.
limitations: No current executive/administrative/professional salary threshold, independent-contractor or joint-employer conclusion.
Federal fact sheets are scoped guidance; current state/local obligations and all compensation components require separate review.

title: Assign safety responsibilities before the first customer-site job
description: Separate the employer’s legal duties from brand support and customer procurement conditions.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the job and the employer
paragraphs: Section 5 sets the employer’s general duty and duty to comply with applicable standards. A partner-operated cleaning or maintenance business needs an actual safety system for its work, not simply a clause saying “the operator handles safety.” Identify who employs and directs each worker and where the work occurs before allocating tasks.

sections.heading: Separate three sources of obligations
paragraphs: Applicable law, a customer’s site rules and the brand’s operating standards can overlap but are different records. The OSHA employer-responsibilities overview covers safe workplaces, applicable standards, hazard information and training. A customer’s insurance certificate or induction card is not evidence that every legal standard has been met.
bullets: List chemicals, equipment, access conditions and foreseeable task hazards.
Identify the relevant federal OSHA or state-plan authority and task-specific standards.
Name who supplies equipment, conducts training, authorises work and responds to incidents.

sections.heading: Fictional example: remote support, local delivery
paragraphs: A foreign facilities brand trains a U.S. partner remotely. The partner’s team will work at a customer site using powered equipment. The practical output is an employer/site/hazard map with missing training and equipment evidence, plus questions about each entity’s actual control. The brand’s remote location does not decide the legal employer analysis, and this guide does not make that determination.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Before the first job, the local operating lead should hold dated training, equipment and site-permission evidence and a clear escalation route. Keep unresearched standards and state-plan differences visible as unresolved tasks.

practicalOutput: An employer/site safety responsibility map and evidence checklist for the first job.
limitations: No task-specific OSHA standard, state-plan rule, incident-reporting deadline or joint-employer determination has been researched here.

title: Give the local employer an I-9 timing and retention owner
description: A foreign owner staying abroad still needs an operational hire-verification workflow in the U.S. business.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Assign the operational role
paragraphs: The entity hiring the employee needs a verification process even when the parent company and owner remain overseas. Section 274a.2(b)(1) sets employee and employer timing. The employee completes Section 1 at hire; the employer generally examines the required evidence and completes Section 2 within three business days of hire. For employment of less than three business days, the employer examination/completion occurs at hire.

sections.heading: Do not improvise a remote procedure
paragraphs: The regulation recognises physical examination or an alternative procedure authorised under its specified provision. That reference does not make every video call, scanned passport or overseas manager review sufficient. Obtain the current official form, acceptable-document instructions and any authorised alternative-procedure conditions before using the process. The USCIS instruction PDF returned HTTP 403 during this review; its current edition and detailed procedure remain unverified here.

sections.heading: Retention depends on both dates
paragraphs: For an employer, §274a.2(b)(2)(i) requires retention for three years after hire or one year after employment ends, whichever is later. In a fictional example, a hire on January 15, 2027 and termination on January 15, 2030 produces a later retention endpoint of January 15, 2031. This illustration is not a live personnel record or a conclusion about another retention duty.

sections.heading: Output and privacy
paragraphs: Create a task register with hire dates, verification owner, completion evidence and retention calculation. Keep identity documents and completed forms in the employer’s controlled personnel system; do not put them in this site’s planning notes. Track any current-form or remote-procedure question as unresolved until the official instructions can be checked.

practicalOutput: A hire-verification calendar and retention worksheet without identity-document uploads.
limitations: Current USCIS form edition and detailed acceptable-document/remote-procedure instructions could not be read because the PDF returned 403.
No individual work-authorisation, anti-discrimination, E-Verify or immigration-category determination.

title: Name the importer of record before shipping branded equipment or stock
description: A freight quote and a delivery term do not replace the legal-party and recordkeeping check.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Separate the commercial and legal roles
paragraphs: For a launch shipment, identify the seller, purchaser, owner, consignee, proposed importer of record, customs broker and ultimate recipient. Section 1484 requires the importer-of-record entry/completion information using reasonable care. Its eligible-filer language includes the owner or purchaser and an appropriately designated licensed person under the stated conditions. A carrier’s or forwarder’s name on a quote does not alone answer those roles.

sections.heading: Collect the entry evidence before dispatch
paragraphs: Section 141.11 addresses evidence of the right to make entry through specified shipping-document arrangements. Link those records with the commercial invoice, actual product description, classification, value, origin and any product-agency requirements. The broker needs accurate underlying facts; outsourcing filing is not a substitute for defining the responsible parties.

sections.heading: Use a category-specific retention schedule
paragraphs: Section 163.4 generally uses five years from entry or the activity that created the record, but lists exceptions, including particular drawback, packing-list, informal consignee and carrier records. Do not set every customs document to “five years” without identifying its category and any other applicable rule.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: An overseas brand sends demonstration machines to a partner and assumes the partner’s warehouse will handle importation. Before dispatch, operations should obtain the actual importer/broker authority, product and value evidence, intended use and return/disposal plan. A shipment-role sheet should record each document owner and unresolved customs or product requirement. No shipment is cleared by this example.

practicalOutput: A shipment-role and customs-evidence sheet with a category-specific retention owner.
limitations: No product classification, customs value, bond, nonresident-importer eligibility or agency admissibility determination.

title: Build a dated tariff evidence ledger instead of guessing an all-in rate
description: Start with the exact product and legal schedule before putting a duty percentage into unit economics.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A product name is not a tariff classification
paragraphs: Describe materials, function, composition, dimensions and how the goods are presented at entry. USITC’s HTS help explains the classification framework and access to legal notes and CBP ruling resources. A similar catalogue label can hide a legally significant product difference. Keep a proposed code labelled proposed until the relevant analysis is done.

sections.heading: Keep base and additional duties separate
paragraphs: The schedule contains legal notes and Chapter 99 provisions that may affect the calculation. Record the schedule version/date, candidate classification, country facts, any claimed preference and each additional-duty or exclusion question. This guide does not quote a current rate or conclude which temporary measure applies.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two cleaning machines
paragraphs: A brand plans to ship a powered scrubber and a replacement battery. Treating the combined shipment as “cleaning equipment at 5%” leaves the product distinctions, classification and any additional measures untested. The finance model should show the duty cells as unknown until supported, and test a clearly labelled estimate separately from a verified rate.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Give the customs reviewer a product evidence pack and a dated rate ledger, with the authority, scope, effective date, unresolved issue and person responsible for each entry. Recalculate landed cost when a product, supplier, origin or legal provision changes.

practicalOutput: A product-specific classification and tariff evidence ledger feeding the landed-cost model.
limitations: Workflow only: no current tariff rate, temporary measure, exclusion, product code or origin preference has been substantively verified.

title: Separate origin marking from tariff and brand nationality
description: Trace manufacturing steps before labelling an imported product with the headquarters country.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Which origin question are you answering?
paragraphs: Brand ownership, shipping point, country-of-origin marking and preferential tariff origin are distinct questions. For the marking part, §134.1(b) starts with manufacture, production or growth and addresses further work that effects substantial transformation. It expressly points to part 102 for the relevant NAFTA/USMCA-country marking cases. Do not replace that framework with “our company is incorporated in Singapore.”

sections.heading: Use the general marking rule with its limits
paragraphs: Section 134.11 states that foreign-origin articles, or their containers as applicable, generally need a conspicuous, legible, indelible and sufficiently permanent English country name indicating origin to the ultimate U.S. purchaser. The part contains exceptions and special rules. A general quotation does not settle whether this product, container or downstream processing qualifies for an exception.

sections.heading: Fictional example: assembly in a second country
paragraphs: A European brand buys components in one country and assembles its equipment in another before shipment to the United States. A “European brand” sticker does not establish the manufacturing-origin answer. Operations should document each process, materials and product state before/after assembly, then obtain a product-specific marking analysis. This guide makes no substantial-transformation finding.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Keep a manufacturing-origin map, proposed artwork and evidence question for each product. Link the marking conclusion to the tariff ledger without assuming they apply the same test. Recheck when the supplier or production steps change.

practicalOutput: A manufacturing-origin map and proposed-marking review pack, separate from tariff preference.
limitations: No product-specific origin determination, marking exception, part102 analysis, preferential eligibility or trade-remedy result.

title: Identify the food FSVP importer before the first shipment
description: The customs broker, FDA registration contact and FSVP importer are not interchangeable roles.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Name the legally defined importer
paragraphs: Under §1.500, the FSVP importer is the U.S. owner or consignee of the food offered for import. If none exists at entry, it is a U.S. agent or representative of the foreign owner or consignee, with the required signed consent. The roles can differ from the customs importer, freight forwarder or foreign facility registration contact; map them rather than assuming one broker performs all of them.

sections.heading: A supplier certificate is not the whole program
paragraphs: Section 1.502 generally requires a program for each imported food, subject to the rule’s scope. FDA’s overview describes qualified individuals, hazard analysis, supplier evaluation, appropriate verification, corrective action and reevaluation. The required verification depends on the food and supplier; do not assume every case needs the same audit or that a certificate automatically suffices. Keep the practical matrix at food-and-foreign-supplier level so a changed supplier is visible for reassessment; this is not a claim that a separate physical document is always required.

sections.heading: Check scope and the entry data
paragraphs: Part 1 contains exemptions and modified requirements, including specified USDA-regulated meat, poultry and egg products. “Exempt from FSVP” does not mean unrestricted food importation. Section 1.509 requires importer name, email and an FDA-acceptable unique facility identifier at each line entry and, where relevant, designation before import. Exact category, labelling, prior notice, facility registration and other admissibility duties remain separate questions.

sections.heading: Fictional example and output
paragraphs: A training brand sends a branded packaged snack to its U.S. partner for resale. Before shipment, the supply lead must identify the food and supplier, actual U.S. purchaser at entry, FSVP owner, program evidence and separate food requirements. No “small sample” or “small business” exemption is assumed. Produce a food/party/program matrix with unresolved category questions.

practicalOutput: A food-specific FSVP role and program evidence matrix before shipment.
limitations: No complete food-category, hazard, small-importer, dietary-supplement, labelling, prior-notice, facility-registration or USDA import analysis.

title: Search U.S. trademark rights beyond an exact federal name match
description: Give the brand owner a dated clearance evidence pack before a partner invests in signs or software.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: An exact federal match is only one search
paragraphs: USPTO explains that a comprehensive search looks for confusingly similar marks for the same or related goods and services. Spelling, sound, appearance and meaning can matter. Federal registered and pending records are important, but state records and common-law use can also matter. A clean exact-name result is not a conclusion that the name is available.

sections.heading: Scope the search to the real U.S. offer
paragraphs: List the word mark, logo, abbreviations, translations and proposed goods/services. Search relevant related services and channels, not only the brand’s current home-country category. Preserve result identifiers, status, owner, apparent use and the date checked.
bullets: Separate registered/pending records from observed marketplace use.
Record similar names and related services, even where the spelling differs.
Keep gaps, uncertain use dates and geographic limitations visible.

sections.heading: Fictional example: facilities brand enters software
paragraphs: A facilities-services brand plans to license both its name and a scheduling app in the United States. A home-market registration and an exact federal search in cleaning services do not settle related software/service conflicts. The practical output is a search pack covering the actual offer, with competing uses and questions assigned for review before signage and app rollout.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: The brand owner should retain a dated clearance brief, the search scope, results and unresolved risks. A partner’s contract acknowledgement is not a substitute for investigating the rights being licensed. Registration strategy, ownership chain and quality-control terms remain separate tasks.

practicalOutput: A dated U.S. mark-search brief covering variants, related services and non-federal use.
limitations: No legal clearance, likelihood-of-confusion finding, registration guarantee, ownership-chain audit or licence quality-control determination.

title: Transfer operating know-how with evidence of secrecy and lawful access
description: An NDA alone does not establish that every manual page is a protected trade secret.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Identify the information and the measures
paragraphs: Section 1839 does not treat everything called confidential as a trade secret.
