sections.heading: Separate the absence of reportable transactions from the absence of a return
paragraphs: The official guidance says that if none of its named transaction categories occurs in the period, a Control Statement is not submitted, but the VAT-return obligation is unaffected. Have finance document the category assessment before treating a period as having nothing to file.

The source also distinguishes changes before the due date from corrections after it. Maintain a correction log linked to the actual reporting period, and obtain the current filing/correction instructions for the entity. This guide does not reproduce the page’s historic monetary-sanction table.

sections.heading: Fictional example: American sales with Czech operating purchases
paragraphs: A Czech VAT-registered service company has one U.S. support customer but also receives local supplier invoices on which it claims input VAT. Finance first classifies the support transaction rather than guessing its place of supply. It separately checks the local inputs against the Control Statement categories; an overseas sales focus has not made those purchase records disappear.

Submission acknowledgements and dated correction log

title: A Greek controller’s U.S. support incident: prepare the breach decision and filing route

The authority describes notification without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours after controller awareness when the risk threshold is met. sections.heading: Do not wait for a complete investigation to identify the filing route
paragraphs: HDPA says incomplete information can be submitted initially and then supplemented without undue delay. The authority’s English/email alternative has stated conditions for cross-border/extraterritorial cases and controllers not established in Greece who cannot use Taxisnet. It is not an unrestricted alternative to the portal for every Greek controller.

sections.heading: Limited VAT liability does not mean full input-tax recovery
paragraphs: For a triggered registration, the board describes an application within three working days from the obligation date. Plan the status review before receiving the service rather than discovering it at year end.

sections.heading: Fictional example: an early-stage brand buys U.S. launch support

title: A Latvian goods shipment for a U.S. pilot: keep export proof and advance dates

sections.heading: An export claim needs the supporting evidence
paragraphs: The current Latvian VAT Law applies a zero rate to goods exports in Section 43(1), while Section 51 denies the rate where the registered taxpayer cannot produce the required export or other zero-rate evidence. The law leaves documentary categories to Cabinet rules. A U.S. billing address or bank payment is not the complete evidence decision.

Define the actual goods transaction, seller, consignee and route. Obtain the current required documentary list and reconcile the invoice, actual movement and relevant export records before relying on the zero rate. This guide has not verified that complete Cabinet list or the U.S. import result.

sections.heading: Advance receipts create a separate timing check
paragraphs: Section 51(4) addresses an advance for a stated zero-rate transaction where goods have not been dispatched or services started within six months. Section 51(5) contains exceptions, including specified contract-based goods with a longer technological manufacturing process and supplies/services already started when the advance is received.

Record the actual advance and dispatch/start dates, plus evidence for any claimed exception. Do not apply the six-month statement without reading those qualifications or copy goods-export treatment onto an ordinary service fee.

sections.heading: Fictional example: a pilot includes branded service equipment
paragraphs: A Latvian maintenance brand supplies equipment to a U.S. operator and receives an advance while production is being arranged. Finance keeps the equipment transaction separate from training/support fees and creates an advance-aging entry. The logistics lead assembles the required export evidence for the actual movement; the tax lead checks timing and any manufacturing exception before confirming treatment.

rows: Exact goods, seller, consignee, price and payment terms
Actual route/movement and required current export documents
Invoice, advance receipt and shipment/start reconciliation
Section 51 conditions and documented exception if relevant
Separate importer, classification, tariff and regulated-product workstream

sections.heading: Use the current language version consciously
paragraphs: Likumi.lv explicitly labels its English translation as outdated, with validity ending in 2024 and later amendments omitted. This explanation uses the relevant current Latvian sections, summarised in English with AI assistance. The old English text is retained only as a currency warning. Temporary movements, goods without a taxable sale, complete documentary categories and U.S. import requirements remain outside this review.

title: A Lithuanian U.S. rollout: classify documents before filling i.SAF

sections.heading: One American supplier folder can contain different document types
paragraphs: VMI’s KM1945 answer distinguishes issued VAT invoices, received foreign documents creating a Lithuanian VAT-accounting obligation, customs declarations and ordinary proformas. It does not treat every record associated with an American counterparty as the same kind of VAT-register entry.

For foreign purchases, first determine whether the actual document and transaction create a Lithuanian VAT-accounting obligation. The guidance distinguishes those required entries from foreign-VAT documents without such an obligation, whose inclusion may be optional under the stated classification rules. The supplier’s nationality alone does not decide this.

sections.heading: Keep proformas, customs evidence and the final return distinct
paragraphs: The same VMI table separates a VAT invoice documenting an actual advance from a free-form request for advance payment that is not a VAT invoice. It also says customs import declarations are not registered as VAT invoices in this invoice register. Preserve those customs records in their own evidence workstream.

VMI’s cited currency answer specifies EUR taxable and VAT amounts. Its reconciliation answer explains that preliminary declarations based on register data can require additional taxpayer information and that register/return differences can arise from timing and corrections. Reconcile the outputs; do not overwrite one simply to make totals look identical.

sections.heading: Fictional example: software, a deposit request and imported equipment
paragraphs: A Lithuanian VAT filer buys U.S. software, receives a proforma requesting an equipment deposit and later imports equipment. Finance classifies the software’s actual VAT obligation, checks whether an advance VAT invoice exists and keeps the customs declaration outside the invoice-register document category. It retains the original currency evidence and the EUR reporting workpaper for applicable entries.

Foreign-purchase Lithuanian-VAT obligation and applicable code
Actual advance VAT invoice versus proforma request
EUR workpaper, timing/correction bridge and return reconciliation

sections.heading: Source and scope limits
paragraphs: The official Lithuanian KM1945 answer is dated 10 July 2025; the cited currency/reconciliation answers are dated 22 November 2018. This is an AI-assisted English summary of those specific current-hosted answers. Actual VAT status/place, classification codes, period, filing cutoff and later changes need review. U.S. tax and franchise or work permissions are separate.

title: Idaho equipment partners: service rights can trigger dealer protections
description: Check the actual sale/service agreement, the combined large-dealer exclusion and the right notice branch before changing a local equipment relationship.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: A service model can cross into this equipment law
paragraphs: Idaho Chapter 28-24 is not confined to a contract labelled a farm franchise. Its dealer-agreement definition includes express or implied, oral or written arrangements granting the right to sell, distribute or service the supplier’s equipment in a continuing commercial relationship. The dealer definition requires the relevant primarily retail sale and/or service business in Idaho. Ordinary cleaning work using a machine does not automatically meet those facts.

sections.heading: Map the equipment and the exclusion together
paragraphs: The chapter includes specified outdoor-power, industrial and construction equipment as well as agricultural uses. Its large industrial/construction-dealer exclusion is conjunctive: the stated primary-business condition, 75% or more of total new product inventory bought from one supplier, and annual average sales exceeding $20 million with that supplier over the preceding 3 years for the responsible territory. “Construction equipment” alone does not establish the exclusion. Preserve the actual product, business, purchase and sales records.

sections.heading: Notice and cure exceptions are not the same list
paragraphs: Section 28-24-104 requires written notice stating the good-cause reasons. The ordinary branch uses at least 90 days’ advance notice and 90 days to cure; it also prevents the agreement expiring early in the specified circumstances. But the notice exceptions refer to subsection(2)(a)–(e), while cure exceptions refer to(a)–(d). Do not mark both periods inapplicable merely because one exception is alleged. Read the actual ground, evidence and separate clauses before action.

Market-penetration action under 104(3) has a different sequence: a one-year advance notice and reasonable supplier assistance, followed by the specified 180-day notice if the required conditions remain. A generic underperformance letter does not identify which track applies. Good cause, comparably applied requirements and the actual competitive change are separate factual questions.

sections.heading: Renewal and territory changes need their own entry
paragraphs: Section 103 addresses coerced amendments, substantial-renovation conditions and other supplier conduct. Section 104A requires notice to identified existing dealers when a new dealership is established or relocated: assigned-area facts matter; the 75-mile alternative applies when no area is assigned. That notice is not a declaration of an exclusive territory or a presale franchise filing. Keep the agreement and dealer-network map together.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: repair rights join the brand licence
paragraphs: Fictional example: an overseas equipment brand authorises an Idaho partner to retail and service its grounds-care line, then proposes a new nearby dealer and replacement after weak sales. The team first tests the statutory equipment/dealer facts and exclusion, then maps the new-dealer notice and performance process independently. The example does not classify an actual operator or prove a right to terminate.

sections.heading: Build the relationship-change file
bullets: List the actual machines, product uses, retail/service rights and legal entities.
Test every element of the combined exclusion with actual period and supplier records.
Identify the exact proposed action, cause, comparators and separate notice/cure exception lists.
Keep market-penetration assistance, inventory availability and communications where that branch applies.
Map assigned areas and required new/relocated-dealer notifications.
Check agreement dates/applicability, dispute provisions, federal franchise rules and independent state sales obligations separately.

practicalOutput: Equipment-scope, dealer-network and relationship-change evidence file
limitations: Idaho Chapter 28-24 only; no general franchise registration/disclosure or all-industry relationship conclusion.
No actual dealer status, exclusion, cause, competitive change or termination is determined.

title: Colorado equipment dealers: choose the product and default branch before changing terms
description: Use the 2026 Farm Equipment Fair Dealership Act to distinguish covered light-industrial equipment, cause, notice exceptions and renewal renovation demands.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The title does not settle the product scope
paragraphs: Colorado Article 38 includes machines designed/adapted and used for stated agricultural, horticultural, light-industrial, utility and outdoor-power purposes. It expressly excludes earthmoving and heavy construction, mining and forestry equipment. The dealer must be primarily engaged in retail equipment sale. A maintenance brand must map the actual goods and business, rather than assume every equipment service relationship is covered.

sections.heading: A contract label does not settle the covered agreement
paragraphs: Section 35-38-102 includes oral and written dealer agreements of definite or indefinite duration prescribing equipment purchase/sale rights and obligations. Section 110 has agreement-date/change applicability and makes foreign-law/venue clauses void with respect to an otherwise enforceable article claim. That limited condition matters: this guide does not declare every foreign-law clause invalid or determine an actual dispute.

sections.heading: Cause is separate from the 180-day branch
paragraphs: The Act prohibits covered termination, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes without cause. Section 104 provides a 180-day written notice and cure route, but expressly excepts the first 10 grounds in subsection(2)(b). Those grounds include specified agreement failures, payment and other events. Do not turn the 180-day figure into an unconditional period for every default. Identify the precise cause, supporting facts, comparably applied terms and notice exception before acting.

For the branch that does require that notice, the notice must give the reasons and 180-day cure information. The section protects the stated cure period from early expiry or competitive change without written consent. A sales-target, staffing or licensing issue must be matched to the actual clause, not selected by whichever deadline is shortest.

sections.heading: A renewal renovation is a separate commitment
paragraphs: Section 103(1)(d) restricts requiring substantial renovation or new/additional premises as a renewal/extension condition unless the supplier gives at least one-year written notice, all grounds, and a reasonable completion period after that year. Finance should not fund a new location on the assumption that the renewal clause alone settles these conditions. Preserve the demand and timing independently of an exit notice.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: a new showroom and a missed target
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign outdoor-power supplier asks its Colorado retail dealer to add premises at renewal and threatens replacement for weak sales. Management prepares two records: the renovation demand and its notice/grounds, and the cause/notice branch for the performance action. If the line instead consists of excluded heavy construction equipment, this article is not established as the source of those rights; other law remains a separate question.

sections.heading: Prepare a product-and-action matrix
bullets: Describe actual equipment uses and exclusions; document the primarily retail business.
Identify the supplier, dealer agreement and relevant agreement/change dates.
Match the stated cause to 104’s precise ground and exception set.
Keep comparative requirements, notices and cure evidence.
Record renovation/new-space demands, notice, supporting grounds and time to complete.
Leave other sector laws, general franchise sales, inventory valuation and actual litigation outcomes unresolved until reviewed.

practicalOutput: Colorado product-scope and cause/renewal-action matrix
limitations: Only Colorado 35-38 definitions and named relationship provisions; excluded machines do not establish absence of other protection.
No actual scope, cause, notice exception, contract enforceability or renovation condition is decided.

title: Montana motor-dealer data: separate consent from the vendor contract
description: Check the specific motor-vehicle dealer definition, data-sharing consent and transition duties before granting supplier or software access.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The definition changes inside the same statutory part
paragraphs: Montana’s dealer-data provisions use their own definitions in 30-11-717. “Dealer” means the new motor vehicle dealer referenced in 61-4-201, not every construction-equipment retailer covered by other dealership provisions. A standalone repair shop, ordinary service franchise or used-only dealer is not shown to qualify merely by using dealership software. Confirm the actual status first.

sections.heading: A brand contract is not the prescribed data consent
paragraphs: For covered third-party access, the law uses prior express written consent in a document separate from other consent, contract or franchise writings, with identified sharing parties and the required scope/duration detail. Section 718 restricts access, use, sharing and specified technical/contractual interference; it also addresses cyber ransom. Record which legal entity is the manufacturer, data vendor, authorised integrator or other third party because the statutory roles differ.

sections.heading: Do not confuse the two notice clocks
paragraphs: Section 718 allows the prescribed consent to be revoked or amended on 30 days’ notice without cause and immediately for cause. Sections 719–720 separately address vendor/integrator contract termination on the stated 90-day terms and a secure transition to a successor. A longer software-contract term does not, by itself, answer the separate consent question.

The transition provisions address usable electronic data, return/deletion according to the dealer’s written directions, recipient lists and audit access. Plan the export format, successor access and lawful retention before a dispute; an account lockout is not an exit plan.

sections.heading: Required manufacturer data is a scoped branch
paragraphs: Sections 717(9) and 719 distinguish required manufacturer data and specified permitted purposes from broader protected dealer data. The listed purposes include particular transactions, warranty/recall work, performance and other stated functions. Do not treat all manufacturer access as forbidden or all marketing data as automatically required. Map the fields, purpose, source and legal basis. Section 719 also permits the stated compliant push/submission alternative rather than mandatory direct system access.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: the supplier chooses an integrator
paragraphs: Fictional example: a foreign supplier and its Montana new-motor-vehicle dealer use a vendor to exchange warranty and customer information. Before adding a broad customer-marketing feed, the parties identify their roles, separate required manufacturer fields from additional data, document any prescribed consent and plan withdrawal/transition. This example supplies an evidence task, not a conclusion that the feed is lawful.

sections.heading: Build the data-access and exit register
bullets: Verify that the dealer and entities fit these provisions’ definitions.
List data fields, required-manufacturer purposes, recipients and each access method.
Keep the separate consent, duration and revocation instructions.
Record vendor-contract notice separately from consent withdrawal.
Test the successor export format, return/deletion directions, recipient list and audit route.
Check other privacy/security and retention duties; this state branch does not complete them.

practicalOutput: Motor-dealer field/role/consent matrix and secure vendor-transition plan
limitations: Montana 30-11-717–720 and referenced motor-dealer definition only; not general franchise-data or construction-equipment law.
Statutory exceptions and actual roles/purposes require review; no vendor, dataset or transfer is approved.

title: Wyoming equipment exit: turn inventory into a dated eligibility ledger
description: Separate machines, parts, required technology and tools before treating a dealer exit as a cash recovery.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Confirm the relationship before valuing the stock
paragraphs: Wyoming Chapter 40-20 defines the relevant dealer, supplier, equipment and agreement. Dealer status combines selling/leasing to consumers and repairing/servicing equipment, with stated exclusions; mere ownership of a machine is insufficient. A covered location closing can also raise inventory issues under the agreement definition. The separate good-cause/notice branches remain in the Wyoming hub; this guide addresses repurchase evidence.

sections.heading: Use the item’s statutory price basis
paragraphs: Section 120 distinguishes new eligible equipment, qualifying demonstrators and repair parts. Its ordinary figures include 100% of net equipment cost and 95% of current net parts prices for qualifying items, with separate handling/freight and demonstrator conditions. Net equipment cost and current net parts price are defined terms, not simply book value or the latest retail quote.

title: Montenegro invoices: choose the applicable VAT text before the U.S. recipient rule

sections.heading: Publication and application are different dates
paragraphs: Montenegro published a new VAT Act in Gazette 104/2026 in July 2026. Its final provisions distinguish entry into force from application: Article 213 links application to EU accession, while Article 212 links repeal of the older act to the start of that application. The Tax Administration’s July notice repeats that condition.

The Council of the EU’s 6 November 2026 release still describes continuing accession negotiations and provisional chapter closures. That dated status does not fix a future accession date or itself trigger the new VAT law’s application.

sections.heading: For services, identify the recipient and the actual receiving establishment
paragraphs: In the government-hosted consolidation through Gazette issue 12/2026, Article 17 starts with the taxable recipient’s establishment, including the branch for an actual receiving fixed establishment elsewhere. It separately treats non-taxable recipients. A U.S. billing address alone is therefore not the full analysis.

sections.heading: Fictional example: two contracts, different place questions

Taxable status and actual receiving establishment

title: Moldova: distinguish an export-collection account from general U.S. treasury

sections.heading: Start with whose account it is
paragraphs: Article 13 of Moldova’s Foreign Exchange Regulation Law concerns resident accounts at non-resident banks. Record the legal account holder, bank and account type. A Moldovan parent’s own proposed foreign account should not be treated as the same fact as its separately incorporated U.S. subsidiary’s account; the subsidiary’s residence and other rules need their own analysis.
The general branch requires NBM authorization, subject to listed exceptions. Convenience, customer preference or an international expansion plan is not itself one of those exceptions.

sections.heading: The export-collection exception is purpose-limited
paragraphs: The current Romanian consolidation includes Article 13(5)(b1), added in 2025: a resident’s account for collecting sales proceeds from goods and/or services exclusively for export, with final crediting to accounts at licensed banks in Moldova. That is a money-flow condition to build into operations, rather than a general permission to retain an overseas treasury balance.

Another exception concerns direct-investment or real-estate accounts where foreign law makes the investor’s own account compulsory. A bank offering a convenient account does not establish that legal requirement. Article 13(6) also allows further NBM conditions on operations, balances and retention.

sections.heading: Fictional example: American customers want a local collection account
paragraphs: A Moldovan services supplier considers an account in its own name to collect U.S. customer payments. title: Separate the contractor rule, enforcement policy and tax test
description: Prepare actual worker facts without treating a label, a proposed rule or an agency enforcement choice as one universal test.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Use a status table before a factor checklist
paragraphs: As reviewed on November 12, 2026, the current eCFR Part 795 still displays the 2024 economic-reality interpretation. It uses the whole activity and six nonexclusive factors; no single factor or subset is necessarily dispositive. The May 1, 2025 WHD bulletin tells investigators not to apply that analysis in its stated scope and expressly says it does not change employees’ rights or employers’ responsibilities. Investigation policy using 2008 Fact Sheet 13, subject to scope/discretion
A repeal, private-right waiver or closed-case reopening

paragraphs: Record who sets prices/schedules, accepts jobs, hires helpers, buys entrepreneurial assets, markets to others and bears a genuine opportunity for profit or loss. paragraphs: IRS guidance groups common-law evidence into behavioural control, financial control and the type of relationship. paragraphs: In its January 9, 2025 Colt & Joe Trucking opinion/order, the New Mexico district court found that the challenger lacked standing and explained that its arguments would otherwise fail or were waived. title: A brand control clause does not answer every joint-employer test
description: Separate the current NLRA text from FLSA duties, proposed changes and actual employment conduct.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: The current NLRA rule was actually restored
paragraphs: The NLRB’s February 27, 2026 final action says the 2023 rule never took effect after district-court vacatur and restores the 2020 text immediately. Current § 103.40 matches that action: substantial direct and immediate control over one or more listed essential employment terms is central; indirect or unexercised reserved authority has the rule’s qualified supplementary role. This is the NLRA inquiry, not a rule for every employment statute.

sections.heading: Read the documented court step accurately
paragraphs: The Chamber of Commerce v. NLRB opinion/order was ordered March 8, 2024 and filed as Document 47 on March 18. Its remedy discussion states that a final judgment will vacate the 2023 replacement and its removal of the earlier text. The 2026 final rule independently confirms the resulting current regulatory action. This guide does not treat the district opinion as a complete current docket search or a ruling that a brand can never be an employer.

sections.heading: FLSA liability did not disappear with a reserved CFR part
paragraphs: Current FLSA Part 791 is reserved. DOL’s April 23, 2026 joint-employer publication is a proposed rule; its proposed factors and franchise examples must not be applied as an effective safe harbour. The source’s background distinguishes the 2020 FLSA rule, its rescission and litigation history from the NLRA framework. Actual governing FLSA court law and the employment facts still matter.

sections.heading: A real agency example: two businesses sharing a worker
paragraphs: DOL Opinion Letter FLSA2025-05 concerns a restaurant and members club with represented shared operations, managers and workers. On those stated facts, DOL concluded the worker’s hours had to be combined and both employers were responsible for FLSA compliance. The letter expressly limits itself to the supplied facts. Separate incorporation or payroll systems alone did not answer that actual agency inquiry; the letter is not a judgment about all network operators.

sections.heading: Output: a control and hours map
paragraphs: For each entity, record who actually selects workers, sets pay and individual schedules, supervises how work is done, disciplines and terminates. Keep ordinary brand/service standards and employment decisions in separate columns, including any mixed-purpose control. Add shared-worker hours and management evidence. Ask the NLRA, FLSA and relevant state questions separately; the franchise-definition analysis is another workstream.

practicalOutput: An entity/worker control-and-hours map with separate NLRA, FLSA and state questions.
limitations: No joint-employer finding, full circuit survey, bargaining-unit analysis or state-law clearance.
The 2026 FLSA proposal is not an effective franchise exemption or a substitute for current governing law.

title: Assign the consumer-product certificate and safety-reporting jobs
description: Check the actual product, responsible importer and 2026 eFiling phase before shipping branded equipment or stock.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the product and intended use
paragraphs: The consumer-product definition and exclusions require an actual scope check. A B2B invoice, brand licence or equipment label does not decide the question. Identify the article, ordinary users, intended use, materials and other applicable agencies. This guide addresses the CPSC certificate/reporting pathway; it does not establish an electrical, machinery, food, pesticide or workplace standard for an unidentified product.

sections.heading: Certification and filing are assigned jobs
paragraphs: For covered imported finished products, Part 1110 defines the importer/certifier role, required certificate data and eFiling process. It allows specified broker/owner/purchaser/consignee allocations, but the identified certifier remains legally responsible for validity, accuracy, completeness and availability. Identify the applicable rules and actual testing basis; buying a certificate template is not compliance. The part also has five-year supporting-record requirements and conditions for access/furnishing.

sections.heading: Use the actual effective phase and policy distinction
paragraphs: The final rule makes its requirements effective July 8, 2026 for most covered products; specified FTZ entries have a January 8, 2027 phase. As of this review, the latter date is future. CPSC’s FAQ describes an initial policy of not seeking entry denial solely for missing eFiling data while continuing certificate enforcement. That enforcement description is not an exemption, a guaranteed entry outcome or permission to ignore applicable safety rules.

sections.heading: Keep a separate incident/reporting route
paragraphs: Under 15 USC § 2064(b), reasonably supported noncompliance, a potentially substantial product hazard or unreasonable serious-injury/death risk can trigger immediate reporting by the covered firms. Section 1115.14 interprets immediate as 24 hours, with its weekend/holiday computation, and warns against waiting for complete risk estimates. A reasonable investigation is not automatic permission to delay once reportable information is known. Name who receives complaints, preserves evidence and escalates promptly; a supplier’s promise to handle it does not answer every entity’s duty.

sections.heading: Output
paragraphs: Build a product/jurisdiction/standard/certifier matrix and a linked complaint-to-reporting workflow before distribution. Leave unverified standards, test exclusions, fees and authorisations unresolved. Obtain the actual product-specific evidence before dispatch and repeat the check when product, supplier, use or rule changes.

practicalOutput: A product-scope and certificate-responsibility matrix plus a complaint/reporting escalation workflow.
limitations: No particular product jurisdiction, standard/test result, approval, recall decision or shipment clearance.
CPSC import overview returned 403; current certification rule/final action/FAQ and actual statutes were readable and used instead.
eFiling enforcement language is time-sensitive and does not waive the underlying certificate or safety requirements.

title: Test the federal data-security gate before overseas access
description: Map actual data, volumes, people and agreements; an overseas support login can matter even without a file download.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Map access, not only transmission
paragraphs: Part 202 defines access broadly enough to include reading, viewing, editing or otherwise receiving data through systems and cloud platforms. The first screen is the actual U.S. person, foreign/covered person, data, volume and agreement. A remote support account may matter even if the database stays in the United States. Conversely, a foreign address alone does not establish a prohibited transaction.

sections.heading: Use the real data and party thresholds
paragraphs: The rule separates government-related data, which has specified regardless-of-volume criteria, from bulk U.S. sensitive personal data. Bulk aggregation uses the preceding 12 months and the specified same-party conditions, not a per-invoice reset. Exact category thresholds say more than 100 U.S. persons for human genomic data, more than 1,000 for other human-omic/biometric data, more than 1,000 U.S. devices for precise geolocation, more than 10,000 persons for health/financial data, and more than 100,000 persons for covered identifiers. Mixed datasets have their own rule. These counts alone are not a safe harbour for government-related data or other laws.

sections.heading: Do not substitute citizenship or an OFAC result
paragraphs: Part 202’s countries-of-concern and covered-person definitions include their own ownership, organisation, employment, primary-residence and designation rules. The current list names China, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia and Venezuela; China has its stated Hong Kong/Macau definition. Citizenship alone is not the complete test. An OFAC name result is not the same determination, and an unlisted entity can still meet a defined category.

sections.heading: Separate prohibition, restriction and exemption
paragraphs: Data brokerage and specified human-omic transactions have prohibitions; relevant vendor, employment and investment transactions may be restricted subject to the actual security and other conditions. Corporate-group administrative/ancillary operations have a bounded exemption; an ordinary independent franchise/license partner is not assumed to be a qualifying subsidiary or affiliate. Restricted transactions require the current diligence program and annual audit conditions. Do not replace the prescribed security requirements with controls the business merely believes are equivalent.

sections.heading: Current dates and output
paragraphs: The program took effect April 8, 2025. The operative diligence/audit provisions refer to October 6, 2025; DOJ’s old good-faith enforcement-priority policy ran only through July 8, 2025 and is not continuing grace. Build a data/actor/access/agreement matrix, identify any supported exemption and assign unresolved technical controls and reporting. Keep customer/employee data in authorised systems outside this site.

practicalOutput: A federal DSP data/actor/access/agreement screen with explicit volumes, exemptions and unresolved controls.
limitations: No transaction authorisation, exemption finding, security attestation or complete privacy-law clearance.

title: Minnesota franchise changes: termination and nonrenewal use different tests

reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review
practicalOutput: Action/cause/notice/expiry and transfer evidence matrix

No going-concern valuation or complete commissioner-rule, sector, bankruptcy or judicial analysis.

sections.heading: Define the relationship and the action
paragraphs: First apply 80C.01 and the recognized-classification context in 80C.14 subdivisions 1–2. Then describe whether the proposed action is termination/cancellation, failure to renew, or withholding consent to a transfer. Registration expiry and contract expiry are different events. A calendar label cannot substitute for the actual conduct.

sections.heading: Keep cause apart from the notice exception
paragraphs: Subdivision 3 requires good cause and states a 90-day written notice with all reasons and 60 days from receipt to correct, subject to its separate immediate-effect exceptions. Those exceptions concern specified abandonment, business-related conviction and the prescribed uncured goodwill-default branch. Do not assume every fact in the good-cause list also appears in the immediate-notice list.

Preserve the material/reasonable requirement, what failed, notice contents, actual receipt and correction. The source’s goodwill branch itself requires the prescribed prior cure notice. A clause saying breach permits immediate exit does not establish the statutory facts.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal is not simply termination at expiry
paragraphs: Subdivision 4 separately addresses good-cause/failure-to-correct cases and the route requiring at least 180 days’ advance notice plus the stated opportunity to operate long enough to recover fair market value as a going concern, measured from the failure to renew. Do not replace that language with a guaranteed cash refund or simple initial-fee calculation.

It also prohibits refusing renewal for the purpose of converting the franchisee’s premises to the franchisor’s own operation. Identify the real plan and evidence rather than selecting the word nonrenewal because the term is ending.

sections.heading: A transfer request has another question
paragraphs: Subdivision 5 addresses unreasonably withholding consent where the replacement meets the franchisor’s present qualifications and standards. Keep the proposed buyer’s evidence, current standards and actual reasons for a decision. This is not a declaration that every transfer must be approved.

sections.heading: Fictional decision: expiry during a performance dispute
paragraphs: Fictional example: a service brand plans not to renew an operator after weak results and wants to run the same premises itself. Management records the actual purpose, requirements, cure history and renewal facts before issuing a letter. The exercise does not decide good cause, value or a lawful outcome.

Identify actual conduct: early termination, expiry/nonrenewal or transfer.
Separate good-cause facts from the notice exception relied on.
Record every notice, receipt, cure step and relevant expiry date.
For nonrenewal, preserve the actual purpose and going-concern-operation evidence.
For transfer, retain qualifications, current standards and reasons; obtain an actual decision on the facts.

title: Washington: termination and nonrenewal do not use the same exit rule
description: Build separate cause, cure, compensation and territory records before changing a covered franchise relationship.
reviewStatus: AI-assisted primary-source review; no professional legal review

sections.heading: Start with the actual statutory relationship
paragraphs: RCW 19.100.010 includes oral or written, express or implied arrangements involving a substantially prescribed or suggested marketing plan, brand association and a franchise fee. Required purchases and training can matter; the fee definition contains specific wholesale, property and other exceptions. Insurance and specified motor-vehicle relationships are treated separately. The federal definition and the word licence do not decide this state test.

sections.heading: An exclusive territory needs an actual boundary
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(f) addresses franchisor competition and competitive grants where the agreement provides an exclusive territory, which must be specified in the agreement. Draw the area, national-account carve-outs, online leads and service obligations before promising exclusivity. The provision does not create an exclusive territory for every franchise. Approved-source purchasing and conduct standards have their own reasonableness/business-ground tests.

sections.heading: A termination has a cause and cure analysis
paragraphs: Section 180(2)(j) restricts termination before expiry to good cause. Its ordinary default branch uses written notice and a reasonable cure opportunity that need not be more than 30 days. Where a default cannot reasonably be cured within 30 days, the text separately addresses substantial and continuing cure action initiated within that time. Do not write an unconditional 30-day minimum or an automatic right to terminate on day 31.

sections.heading: Nonrenewal compensation is a different ledger

title: Wisconsin: a registered franchise still needs a Fair Dealership Law review

sections.heading: The operating definition is independent

Its dealership test can involve an express or implied, oral or written agreement granting sale/distribution rights or use of a commercial symbol, with a community of interest. sections.heading: Keep the exclusions visible

sections.heading: Cause, advance notice and cure are separate
paragraphs: Section 135.03 prohibits covered termination, cancellation, nonrenewal and substantial competitive changes without good cause and puts the cause burden on the grantor. Section 135.04 ordinarily requires 90 days’ prior written notice, all reasons and 60 days to rectify a claimed deficiency; timely rectification voids the notice. Insolvency, assignment for creditors and bankruptcy have stated notice exceptions.

For nonpayment, the statute supplies written default notice and 10 days to remedy from delivery or posting. The official civil jury instruction’s comment expressly preserves 90 days’ advance notice for that branch while shortening cure to 10 days. A 10-day demand should not be entered as an automatic day-11 termination date.

sections.heading: Inventory and remedies require their own evidence
paragraphs: Under 135.045, grantor-initiated termination can trigger, at the dealer’s option, repurchase at fair wholesale market value of qualifying inventories sold by the grantor for resale. The section is confined to merchandise bearing an identifying grantor mark; it is not reimbursement for every computer or operating asset. Section 135.06 provides a conditional damages/costs/fees and injunction route. An injury or award is not presumed from this checklist.
